title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: A dish made from eggs cooked without added oil or fat, with cheese added. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins, and minerals, while cheese contributes calcium and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable and versatile foods worldwide.
Cooking without fat preserves the natural taste of eggs and reduces the dish’s calorie count.
The cheese can range from soft cottage cheese to sharp cheddar, altering taste and nutrient profile.
Scrambling technique creates a lighter, airy texture by gently stirring the eggs while cooking.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs contain all essential amino acids, making them a complete protein for muscle and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are high in B12, riboflavin (B2) and folate, which support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds a substantial amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish contains virtually no carbs, fitting well into low‑carb dietary patterns.

items.title: Cholesterol in moderation
items.content: Although eggs contain cholesterol, current research shows moderate intake does not raise blood cholesterol for most people.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may develop an allergy to egg proteins, ranging from skin reactions to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: People with high blood cholesterol should monitor their egg consumption.

items.title: Sodium in cheese
items.content: Choose low‑salt cheeses to avoid excessive sodium intake.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat eggs with a splash of milk or water, stir in grated cheese, salt and pepper. Pour the mixture onto a pre‑heated non‑stick pan and cook over medium heat, gently stirring until the eggs set but remain tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store the cooked omelet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat gently with a little water to restore moisture.
